userStories.title: Classify and stamp terminal advisory recurrence
acceptanceCriteria: classifyRecurrence returns blocking, advisory, demoted, retired, and classified arrays.
Given a warning finding at error threshold with appearances below maxAdvisoryRounds, classifyRecurrence places it in advisory and not retired.
Given a sub-threshold finding whose appearances including the current round meet maxAdvisoryRounds, classifyRecurrence places it in retired and not advisory.
Given an error finding whose appearances including the current round meet maxBlockingRounds + 1, classifyRecurrence places it in demoted and not retired.
When cfg omits maxAdvisoryRounds and a sub-threshold finding has two appearances including the current round, classifyRecurrence retires it using default 2.
Every finding in classified has meta.recurrence.disposition equal to its bucket name: blocking, advisory, demoted, or retired.
A finding in demoted has meta.recurrence.wasBlocking equal to true.
A finding in retired has meta.recurrence.wasBlocking equal to false.
Every finding in classified has meta.recurrence.rounds equal to its prior appearance count plus one.
classifyRecurrence returns classified with one entry per input finding in input order.
When an input finding has no meta, classifyRecurrence leaves that input finding without meta after the call.
When an input finding has an unrelated meta key, its classified entry retains that key alongside meta.recurrence.
When cfg.enabled is false, classifyRecurrence returns an empty retired array.
When cfg.enabled is false, no finding returned by classifyRecurrence carries meta.recurrence.
When cfg.enabled is false, classifyRecurrence partitions findings into blocking and advisory by severity alone, matching its behaviour before this feature.

Given a finding with no acIndex, classifyRecurrence counts prior appearances through the existing file, category, and issue-prefix fingerprint fallback and its disposition is unaffected by the missing acIndex.
When priorIterations is empty, classifyRecurrence returns an empty retired array.
When priorIterations is empty, every classified entry has meta.recurrence.rounds equal to 1.
Given a test-gap finding in a test file at or above the blocking threshold, classifyRecurrence places it in blocking regardless of appearance count.
Given a test-gap finding in a test file below the blocking threshold, classifyRecurrence does not place it in blocking.
When tagCoverageGap is applied to a finding carrying meta.recurrence, it returns a finding carrying that recurrence value and meta.coverageGap equal to true.

routing.reasoning: Focused recurrence module and type updates with behaviorally sensitive compatibility paths.

outOfScope: the wording of the reviewer prompt; the `meta.coverageGap` tag's own semantics, which are unchanged.

userStories.title: Configure advisory recurrence cap
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expose the advisory retirement cap through both review configuration schemas.

**Motivation** — the advisory cap is configuration rather than a literal.

**Approach** — Declare `maxAdvisoryRounds` on both `recurrenceDemotion` schema blocks so the cap is configuration rather than a literal.

**Scope** — In: adversarial and semantic schema defaults, validation, and exact-default assertions. Out: classifyRecurrence runtime fallback belongs to US-001; mapper and operation integration belongs to US-003.

**Interface**
```typescript
maxAdvisoryRounds: z.number().int().min(1).default(2)
```
The semantic schema takes the same field, with its `enabled` default left at `false`.
acceptanceCriteria: When adversarial recurrenceDemotion.maxAdvisoryRounds is unset, schema parsing resolves it to 2.
When semantic recurrenceDemotion.maxAdvisoryRounds is unset, schema parsing resolves it to 2.
When semantic recurrenceDemotion.enabled is unset, schema parsing resolves it to false.
When either review config sets recurrenceDemotion.maxAdvisoryRounds to 0, schema validation rejects it.
When adversarial recurrenceDemotion.maxAdvisoryRounds is 5, schema parsing resolves it to 5.

routing.reasoning: Two additive schema fields and existing exact-default assertions.

modifiedFiles.reason: the test at `:6-9` asserts `expect(parsed.recurrenceDemotion).toEqual({ enabled: true, maxBlockingRounds: 2 })`, and `:10-15` makes the same exact-object assertion for the override case. `toEqual` is exact, so the schema's new `maxAdvisoryRounds` default fails both against a correct implementation. US-002 owns updating them to the new invariant: the parsed object also carries `maxAdvisoryRounds: 2`.

the assertion at `:113` pins `result.data.review.semantic` with `toEqual`, including a nested `recurrenceDemotion: { enabled: false, maxBlockingRounds: 2 }`. The new schema default breaks it against a correct implementation. US-002 owns updating it to the new invariant: the nested object also carries `maxAdvisoryRounds: 2`.

outOfScope: the runtime default `classifyRecurrence` applies when the field is absent from a caller-supplied config object, which US-001 owns.

userStories.title: Persist recurrence stamps through review operations
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Preserve classification stamps through both finding mappers and review-audit output.

**Motivation** — a passing record can carry an `error` finding with no explanation.

**Approach** — Give both LLM finding types an optional `meta`, forward `recurrence` through both mappers' allowlists, and have the review operations persist `classified` as `findings` and fold `retired` into `advisoryFindings`. This is what makes the disposition visible to the audit record (nax#1928) and to the prompt builder (US-003).

**Scope** — In: LLM meta declarations, mapper allowlists, adversarial/semantic classified persistence, retired advisory routing, and recurrence-retired logs. Out: recurrence algorithm and cap default belong to US-001/US-002; prompt rendering and seed filter belong to US-004; changing passed computation is out of scope.

**Interface**
```typescript
meta?: Record<string, unknown>
```
The `result.findings` lane needs no mapper at all: per `semantic-helpers.ts:61-62` and #1861, the review audit persists the **raw op shape**, so a stamp on the LLM finding reaches `ReviewAuditEntry.result.findings` directly through `review-decision.ts:92`.
acceptanceCriteria: When toAdversarialReviewFindings receives an LLM finding with meta.recurrence, it returns a Finding with the same disposition, rounds, and wasBlocking values under meta.recurrence.
When toAdversarialReviewFindings receives an LLM finding with no meta, its returned Finding meta has no recurrence key.
When toAdversarialReviewFindings receives meta.recurrence and verifiedBy, its returned Finding carries both meta.recurrence and meta.verifiedBy.
When llmFindingToFinding receives a semantic LLM finding with meta.recurrence, it returns a Finding with the same recurrence values.
When adversarialReviewOp.verify() accepts findings classified by recurrence, it returns one stamped findings entry per accepted finding.
When adversarialReviewOp.verify() has retired classifications, advisoryFindings includes every retired entry in addition to advisory, demoted, and AC-dropped entries it already carries.
When adversarialReviewOp.verify() classifies retired findings, normalizedFindings contains only blocking entries so retired findings are never routable to the rectification cycle.

Given a warning adversarial finding and sufficient matching priorAdversarialIterations to reach maxAdvisoryRounds, adversarialReviewOp.verify() returns it in advisoryFindings stamped disposition retired.
When classifyRecurrence returns retired findings, adversarialReviewOp.verify() emits one info review log per finding with event review.adversarial.recurrence_retired and its file and category.
When classifyRecurrence returns demoted findings, adversarialReviewOp.verify() still emits one log per finding with event review.adversarial.recurrence_demoted.
When semantic recurrenceDemotion.enabled is true, semanticReviewOp.verify() returns one stamped findings entry per accepted finding.
When semantic recurrenceDemotion uses its false default, semanticReviewOp.verify() returns advisoryFindings entries with no meta.recurrence.

When a review-audit entry is built from adversarial verify output with recurrence stamps, result.findings exposes those values so a passed record distinguishes a demoted error without replaying demotion state.
When an error finding is demoted and blocking is empty, adversarialReviewOp.verify() returns passed equal to true, so the verdict rule is unchanged by this feature.

routing.reasoning: Cross-module raw/audit and mapped data-flow changes with logging and dual operation integration.

outOfScope: the computation of `passed`; enabling `recurrenceDemotion` for semantic-review, whose default stays `false`.

userStories.title: Render retirement acknowledgements and suppress fix seeds
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Keep retired findings visible in history while removing their re-flag mandate and paid fix eligibility.

**Motivation** — The only way to stop a reviewer re-raising a true finding is to keep telling it about the finding.

**Approach** — Render retired findings in an acknowledgement block that forbids re-flagging rather than in the verdict list that mandates it, and stop seeding them into the non-blocking-fix lane.

Both filters key on the stamp US-001 writes, restated here because it is the only shape this story needs from that module: each `Finding` may carry `meta.recurrence = { disposition, rounds, wasBlocking }`, where `disposition` is one of `"blocking"`, `"advisory"`, `"demoted"` or `"retired"`. An entry with no `meta.recurrence` predates this feature and is treated exactly as today.

**Scope** — In: prompt partition, acknowledgement wording, non-retired verdict count, and retired seed exclusion. Out: still-blocking wording remains unchanged; iteration-store retention and advisory reporting remain unchanged; classification and operation stamping belong to upstream stories.

**Interface**
```typescript
export function buildPriorIterationsBlock<F extends Finding>(iterations: Iteration<F>[]): string
export function actionableAdvisoryFindings(findings: readonly Finding[]): readonly Finding[]
```
Retirement is a **rendering** change: the finding stays in the store and stays in the prompt, but moves out of the verdict list — which requires a per-item classification and mandates identical re-flagging — into an acknowledgement block that states it is closed and must not be re-flagged.
acceptanceCriteria: Given an iteration with a finding stamped meta.recurrence.disposition retired, buildPriorIterationsBlock omits that finding from its verdict-required list.
Given an iteration with a retired stamped finding, buildPriorIterationsBlock returns an acknowledgement section naming that finding's file and category.
When buildPriorIterationsBlock renders retired findings, the acknowledgement section states they are closed and must not be re-flagged.
Given iterations whose findings have no meta.recurrence, buildPriorIterationsBlock returns the same block it returned before this feature.
buildPriorIterationsBlock's verdict template counts only findings not stamped retired.
Given an iteration whose findings are all stamped retired, buildPriorIterationsBlock returns no verdict-required list.
Given three consecutive review rounds where a warning is emitted in round 1 and reaches maxAdvisoryRounds in round 2, the round-3 prior-iterations block lists it only in the acknowledgement section.
When actionableAdvisoryFindings receives a finding stamped disposition retired, its returned list omits it.
When actionableAdvisoryFindings receives a finding stamped disposition advisory, its returned list contains it.
When actionableAdvisoryFindings receives actionRequired false or acDropped true findings, its returned list continues to omit them.
When only retired advisory findings are provided to the non-blocking-fix seed path, shouldRunNonBlockingFix receives an advisory count excluding them and no fix pass is dispatched.

routing.reasoning: Two focused consumer filters with prompt formatting and execution-count integration.

modifiedFiles.reason: assertions over the rendered block's finding count and its verdict template. Under AC 1 and AC 5 a retired entry leaves the verdict list and the template count drops accordingly, so any count-based expectation over a fixture containing a stamped entry fails against a correct implementation. US-003 owns updating them to the new invariant: the verdict list and its template count only entries not stamped `disposition: "retired"`, and retired entries appear once in the acknowledgement section.

outOfScope: the run-end advisory report surface, which continues to read `advisoryFindings` and therefore still lists retired findings.

analysis:
This is a cross-cutting enhancement to existing recurrence review flow. `classifyRecurrence` currently has a three-bucket result and returns immediately for disabled configs; when enabled, it checks the severity gate before looking up prior appearances, so advisory findings can never recur or retire (`src/review/recurrence-demotion.ts:137-216`). It already counts history by source and supports both AC-index and prose fallback fingerprints (`src/review/recurrence-demotion.ts:84-131`); preserve that identity logic and test-gap blocking carve-out. The recurrence candidate and configuration types lack `meta` and the advisory-cap field (`src/review/recurrence-demotion.ts:137-158`), while duplicate inline config shapes occur in `src/review/types.ts:132` and `src/review/types.ts:258`. Both schemas currently default only enabled and maxBlockingRounds (`src/config/schemas-review.ts:77-82`, `src/config/schemas-review.ts:135-140`), and operation-level fallbacks likewise need the optional runtime-compatible field behavior (`src/operations/adversarial-review.ts:479`, `src/operations/semantic-review.ts:425`).

The raw LLM finding is the audit lane: both operations currently return `findings: accepted` (`src/operations/adversarial-review.ts:526-539`, `src/operations/semantic-review.ts:457-466`) and review-decision forwards that unprojected shape directly into `result.findings` (`src/execution/story-orchestrator/review-decision.ts:92`). Therefore classification must return cloned, stamped `classified` entries in input order and the operations must use them rather than accepted. Mapper conversion is separately significant: adversarial and semantic mappers rebuild an allowlisted `metaExtras`, so a stamp applied to an LLM finding is currently discarded (`src/review/adversarial-helpers.ts:136-169`, `src/review/semantic-helpers.ts:188-209`). Add optional `meta` to both LLM interfaces and forward only `meta.recurrence`, preserving existing allowlisted keys. Apply existing coverage-gap tagging after conversion, which shallow-merges meta and should coexist with recurrence (`src/review/recurrence-demotion.ts:133-135`).

The prior-iteration prompt maps all stored findings into one verdict-required list and counts all of them in the verdict template (`src/prompts/builders/prior-iterations-builder.ts:47-118`). Retirement must therefore be a rendering partition, not a store deletion: historical unstamped entries remain legacy verdict entries, retired stamped entries need a closed/no-reflag acknowledgement block, and the template total must exclude them. Token-guard collapsed-round counts should remain a consideration because they currently use raw finding counts (`src/prompts/builders/prior-iterations-builder.ts:70-79`). Retired findings remain in advisory reporting but must be excluded only at the non-blocking seed filter, which currently filters actionRequired and acDropped (`src/execution/non-blocking-fix.ts:54-60`); execution-plan computes the downstream count from this filter (`src/execution/story-orchestrator/execution-plan.ts:402`).

Risks are backward compatibility and semantic behavior: maxAdvisoryRounds must stay optional in TypeScript while schema defaults resolve it, disabled mode must be byte-for-byte behaviorally equivalent in partitioning and must not stamp/mutate inputs, and semantic recurrence remains disabled by default. The migration path is additive: legacy stored iterations without `meta.recurrence` continue rendering in verdict lists; retired findings remain stored/reported but cease verdict mandate and fix eligibility. Existing test files identified by the spec are near size limits, so create the two designated sibling test files rather than grow `recurrence-demotion.test.ts` or `non-blocking-fix.test.ts`.
outOfScope: The nax#1910 step-3 analyzer over `review-audit/*.json` — measured 2026-09-10 at 11.1% `unmatched` on 27 sub-threshold findings from a single feature, too small a sample to justify building it.

Retiring a finding on `meta.evidence.status === "unmatched"`. All three `unmatched` findings in the measured corpus were substantive defects, so evidence status measures quote hygiene rather than finding validity and must not gate retirement.
Seeding the non-blocking-fix lane from semantic-review's advisory bucket, tracked as nax#1957 and gated on the nax#1801 ruling.
Changing how `passed` is computed at `adversarial-review.ts:512`. A record carrying `passed: true` beside a demoted `error` keeps that verdict and explains it.
Enabling `recurrenceDemotion` for semantic-review. The schema field is wired, the default stays `false`, and flipping it is a separate decision needing its own baseline.
The "whack-a-mole within a file" failure where each round yields genuinely new findings, tracked as nax#1157.
Excluding `acDropped` findings from the non-blocking-fix seed. That filter at `non-blocking-fix.ts:54-60` is an existing hold on nax#1801 and is left exactly as it stands.
Changing the `still-blocking` instruction at `prior-iterations-builder.ts:115`. Retirement works by moving a finding out of the verdict list, not by softening the instruction that governs the list.
Similarity-clustering or otherwise changing `fingerprintFor`. Retirement inherits whatever recurrence identity that function already provides.
Dropping retired findings from the iteration store or from `advisoryFindings`. They remain stored and remain reported; only their prompt rendering and their fix-lane eligibility change.
